summary:
The project consists of software that adapts in the three main space environments (LEO, Mars and the Moon). It is a visual and highly intuitive system that breaks down the physiological data of the Astronaut with the help of an anatomic model and also a virtual assistant that gives reminders of daily tasks such as drinking water or doing exercises in order to keep an optimal condition.

The project addresses the challenge by including indicators related to each risk mentioned, its importance lies in how it tells the astronaut what to do by having specific recommendations for each situation , such as reducing physical exertion, staying hydrated, or doing guided breathing exercise; It also provides direct access to the related module and for serious cases, autonomous medical protocols provide step-by-step guidance tailored to the environment, designed for use without medical support from Earth.
details:
"Vitalis 360" operates using a self-contained web architecture (a single-page application in a single HTML/CSS/JavaScript file) that processes all physiological logic reactively and locally on the client side without relying on external servers. Its core on JavaScript engine monitors changes in the upper biometric profile and recalculates in real time the metabolic equations (Mifflin-St Jeor), fluid balance, sleep cycles, and training loads, rendering dynamic visualizations using vector graphics to display the anatomy of the human body (SVG), canvases for trabecular microarchitecture, and native audio synthesis (Web Audio API) for the CPR metronome and mission alarms, featuring a total of 16 emergency protocols guided by bilingual text and audio (EN/ES), as well as binary decision trees and an automatic inventory section for medical equipment on the spacecraft.

In terms of aerospace regulatory and physiological support, the system incorporates criteria aligned with the *NASA-STD-3001* standard (Space Flight Human-System Standard) for the preservation of human health in isolated and extreme environments, HRR, and the HRP. This is reflected in the continuous monitoring of bone and muscle mass loss through progressive mechanical loading countermeasures, the regulation of the circadian rhythm (cortisol curve and REM/N3 sleep architecture), strict control of hydration and thermal stress, and phased protocols for immediate medical response (hemorrhage control, life support, and MEDEVAC evacuation) designed for operational crews.

The main advantage it offers is that it operates in a hybrid manner, combining a 100% offline system with an MQTT connection if a route is found, since it has been built for three different scenarios—Orbit, Moon, and Mars—without compromising personalized care for each crew member and providing guided assistance when necessary to preserve the crew’s lives and operational capabilities. We’ve managed to merge clinical physiology, telemetry, and instructional design; instead of presenting static medical tables or lengthy manuals that are difficult to read during a crisis, it converts metabolic equations and emergency protocols into interactive simulations, integrating vector visualization and real-time audio synthesis. In addition, mental health is monitored through a virtual companion named NOVA, who is responsible for reminding crew members of their daily physical and psychological tasks during the mission, including 12 recreational activities.
